statement: A release driver's stage-1 preflight ran 'git fetch --tags' with all output discarded, and 34 of 34 shim tests passed, yet the operator's first real dry run refused (cejel #393, 2026-10-02): the clone held a stale local v1, the one tag that moves every release, and real git refuses to overwrite a changed tag ('would clobber existing tag'). The shim git never refused a fetch, so the failure mode was unrepresentable in the tests, and the driver's own '>/dev/null 2>&1' hid git's explanation. Rule: a fake of an external tool must be able to fail the way the real tool fails on the inputs the product will meet, and every command whose failure refuses must put the tool's stderr in the refusal. Fix by writing the refusing shim case red first, then the code.
